QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_22

question.text: Under SAS-200, the Reduction in Child Stunting indicator requires baseline measurement. If the SE did NOT measure height-for-age at baseline, the SIA should:

answer.text: Silently drop the indicator from the Report
Fabricate a baseline using SE's verbal estimates
Use national NFHS-5 district-level stunting as a proxy baseline and disclose
Use the SE's CSR report narrative as baseline

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Where the SE has no baseline, the SIA can reasonably adopt a PUBLICLY available district-level NFHS-5 figure as proxy baseline — this is a defensible external benchmark. Full disclosure of the proxy source is mandatory. Options B, A, D are either unethical, incomplete or unreliable. **The Trap:** Option B fabricates data. Option A is concealment. Option D relies on self-report narrative. **Cross-Exam Context:** NFHS / SRS proxy-baseline logic mirrors XV (Research Analyst — peer-group benchmarking) and V-B (MF Foundation basics). **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Bookmark the NFHS-5 district fact-sheet PDFs — they carry age/gender-wise stunting, anaemia and ANC coverage data down to district level. That is your instant proxy baseline.
